A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. The appendix text and rendered pages match exactly.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulations comparing Fictitious Play variants, including regret trajectories and means and standard deviations over 100 random initializations (Section 5 and Appendix E).

after.justification: v3 retains these original simulations in Figure 1, Tables 2–3, and Figures 4–6, including the results over 100 random initializations.

M1.justification: The Optimistic Fictitious Play updates in Section 2.2 and Alternating Fictitious Play procedure in Appendix D.2 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Matching Pennies and the same identity, generalized Rock-Paper-Scissors, and random payoff-matrix families. No game family or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains FP, OFP, and AFP. Tables 2–3 and the experimental appendix plots retain the same FP-versus-OFP comparisons.

E3.justification: The 10,000-iteration budget, matrix dimensions, regret metric, initialization procedures, and lexicographical and randomized tiebreaking protocols remain unchanged (Section 5 and Appendix E).

E4.justification: The checks of robustness to tiebreaking rules and random initializations in Section 5 and Appendix E are unchanged. No ablation or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Tables 2–3 retain means and standard deviations over 100 random initializations. Neither the repetition information nor the uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in Tables 2–3 and empirical trajectories in Figures 1 and 4–6 match. No result entries or reported empirical findings are added or removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Assumption 1, regret bounds, energy arguments, and proofs in Sections 2–4 and Appendices A–D remain unchanged. The new introductory remark clarifies cited prior work without adding a derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same constant-regret claim for OFP in two-strategy games, AFP regret lower bound, and suggested extension to higher dimensions.

C2.justification: The geometric mechanism explanation and interpretation of the higher-dimensional simulations are unchanged. Section 5 retains the limitation that proving constant OFP regret for all zero-sum games remains open.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 retains the same matrix constructions, initialization sampling instructions, single-personal-computer description, and statement that experimental code is in the supplementary material.

R1.justification: The Introduction now explicitly states that Daskalakis and Pan (2014) showed the classical O(T^(1−1/n)) FP bound to be tight using adversarial tiebreaking. v2 gave the rate and citation without this qualification; the cited-work set is unchanged.

P1.justification: There is a limited introductory clarification, a small refinement from 'over time' to 'over the time horizon,' and replacement of individual author email lines with a correspondence footnote. The section sequence and substantive exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: The author block changes from two rows to one, and Table 1 moves from page 3 to page 2 beside the contribution summary, causing text reflow. Figure content and table designs remain unchanged; the appendices are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the prior-work discussion more precise by identifying the adversarial-tiebreaking condition behind the cited tight FP bound. Placing Table 1 directly after the contribution summary also improves presentation. These limited clarity gains leave the theoretical arguments, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information unchanged.
